definition.text: Internal indices are unsupervised measures that rely exclusively on information present within the data set.

scope.text: These indices evaluate the quality of a clustering structure without external information and are categorized into measures of cluster cohesion (compactness and tightness) and cluster separation (isolation).

definition.text: A model evaluation method used in supervised classification that aims to make effective use of all labeled instances for both training and testing.

scope.text: Used for model assessment (evaluation) and model selection. Pre-processing operations, such as feature selection or hyper-parameter tuning, should be performed within the training fold of each run rather than on the entire dataset. In some configurations, an inner cross-validation framework is used for model selection while an outer framework is used for model evaluation.
